Subject: Sustained vs Crest throughput: post-call snapshot & sizing asks

Hi Liam / Ellen —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and concrete asks so we can size a realistic pilot cluster: 

Summary of what we heard you need:
- Hard latency target: 95th <= 250ms for single-turn chat (avg prompt length ~220 tokens)
- Streaming use case for live agent-assist with partial token streaming enabled
- Typical steady-state: ~45 QPS (user requests/sec) across US region, expectation of 3x crest for marketing spikes
- Median token output per response: ~160 tokens; peak responses up to 800 tokens when generating summaries

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Wed?):
1) A 48-hour sample of production traffic (CSV) for a typical weekday and a marketing spike window (we referenced a template; attached an example).
2) Clarify whether the 3x crest is simultaneous across all users (global spike) or concentrated to specific endpoints.
3) Any hard concurrent-connection limits on your side for the streaming endpoints (we need to know if your front end multiplexes).

Next steps (from our side):
- Marissa will produce a draft sizing + cost sketch based on the samples (aiming for 1-2 reserved nodes for the pilot).
- Neha will outline the telemetry we need in Prod to validate 95th latency (tracing spans + per-request token counts).

Attachments: fastcart_workload_samples.csv (sample CSV of request timestamps/qps/token_counts), redwood-sizing-proposal-v1.pdf (initial sketch, internal).

If you want to hop on a brief 20-min follow-up tomorrow for the CSV parsing, I can make room.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Connell <liam@fastcart.ai>

Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sustained vs Crest throughput: post-call snapshot & sizing asks

Thanks, Priyom — appreciated. Quick answers inline:

> Hard latency target: 95th <= 250ms
We can commit to that target for the pilot if the model variant stays within the 7B family (we want to avoid larger 30B variants during pilot).

> Streaming use case
Yes — agent-assist streams token-by-token. Front end uses a single websocket per user session; we don't multiplex multiple sessions on the same socket.

> Steady-state: ~45 QPS, 3x crest
The 3x crest is regional/global — typically marketing-driven peaks where all regions see ~3x for a 15-30 minute window. On Tuesday mornings it has spiked to ~2.8x historically.

> Token sizes
We attached a small CSV (will upload to your Drive link) with a day sample and one 20-min crest window.

We don't have a strict concurrent-connection limit beyond the socket-per-session pattern.

We can hop on 20-min tomorrow at 10am PT if that works for Marissa (Ellen and I will join).

—Liam
Lead Platform Engineer, FastCart.ai
liam@fastcart.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Apr 2028 08:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained vs Crest throughput: post-call snapshot & sizing asks

Liam / Priyom — thanks for the file upload. I parsed the sample and pulled a few quick observations for the pilot sizing: 

Quick notes from sample (20-min crest window + one steady-day slice):
- Steady QPS median: 42 QPS (matches your estimate).
- Crest peak observed: 122 QPS (approx 2.9x steady).
- Average tokens per response (crest): 560 (because of summary requests), steady avg: 150.
- Streaming sessions tend to keep sockets open ~3 minutes average; a 15-min crest had 80% of new sessions starting within first 5 minutes.

Sizing draft (pilot, 99th latency safety margin):
- Model: 7B-realtime quantized variant (recommended to meet 250ms 95th).
- Nodes: 3 inference nodes (A100-style) with steady autoscale to 1 extra during crest; continuous batching + KV-cache suggested for repeated prefixes.
- Concurrency: plan for 130 concurrent streaming connections per node (buffers for partial tokens).
- Token throughput target: steady ~45 QPS * 160 tokens = ~7.2k tokens/sec; crest ~122 QPS * 560 tokens = ~68.3k tokens/sec.

Open questions (for your confirm):
1) Is the crest window tolerated to have slightly relaxed latency (e.g., 95th up to 350ms) in exchange for cost savings?
2) Any regulatory requirement to keep traffic inside US-only regions?

I attached a fast first-pass PDF (redwood-sizing-proposal-v1.pdf) — it includes a simple cost estimate and node map. We'll lock numbers after you confirm the two questions above and we get a full 48-hour CSV.

If 10am PT tomorrow works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ellen Wu <ellen.wu@fastcart.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sustained vs Crest throughput: post-call snapshot & sizing asks

Thanks Marissa — that looks good. Quick responses: 

1) We can accept a relaxed crest latency to 350ms 95th during marketing spikes for the pilot. Our SLAs for customers are not strict during campaigns, and prioritizing cost makes sense.
2) Traffic must remain within the US for the pilot (data residency).

Action items we will complete by EOD Monday:
- Upload the full 48-hour CSV to your Drive link (includes steady + two crest windows).
- Provide a short note on expected growth (3-6 months) and whether crest multiple will change.

Please send the calendar invite for 10am PT tomorrow and we will confirm attendees.

Thanks,
